name: What is the difference between patching a kitchen jamb and replacing the whole frame?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between patching a kitchen jamb and replacing the whole frame?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repairing an existing frame preserves existing custom casings, reduces dust, and avoids disrupting adjacent kitchen tile backsplashes or finished drywall. However, if the jamb is rotted or structurally compromised, a patch will only offer temporary relief. Installing a new pre-hung frame or rebuilding the jamb from scratch requires more labor—including removing trim, shimming, refitting the door, and repainting—but delivers a plumb, durable opening that closes properly without ongoing adjustments.
acceptedAnswer.description: Patching preserves custom trim and tile connections with less mess, whereas a full jamb rebuild takes more labor but permanently fixes deep rot, warping, or latch issues.
